“Are you pregnant?!”

Mydei looks to his right: Perdikkas seems to have lost all the color from his face and Ptolemy is fanning him with a piece of paper. He looks to his left: Leonnius is typing on his cell phone as if his life depended on it and Peucesta is pacing in place like a caged lion. 

Look ahead again: the vein on Hephaestion's forehead could very well burst if Mydei doesn't watch his words.

Anyway, “There was no need to make such a fuss.”

The sigh of the pink-haired boy could be heard from here to Xianzhou.

“Mydeimos.” Oh, he's angry. Mydei settled more comfortably in his seat, avoiding putting any weight on his belly. “You've been hiding your pregnancy for almost three months.”

Mydei nodded slowly. He tilted his head slightly to the side the next second. “Yes, it took you a while to realize.”

“That's not the point!” Hephaestion tugged hard at his own hair. He shouldn't; his fans would be devastated if he went bald. “You've been vomiting after every meal! You're always tired after every practice! How could you possibly do a world tour while pregnant?”

Mydei frowns for the first time since this conversation began. “Don't underestimate me. I could.”

“That's not the point either!”

Mydei is really serious here: His father has told him many times about how amazing his wife was when she was pregnant with him. Gorgo flaunted her baby bump like a proud expectant mother, yet she was still the intimidating and powerful boss of Kremnos Corporation for as long as she could before Mydei decided to come out of the shadows.

If his dear mother could do that, then Mydei can continue being the lead guitarist and singer of his rock band while pregnant too.

Leonnius's shaky sigh distracts them both from their argument. When Mydei and Hephaestion look at him, he just points to his phone with a defeated expression.

“Well... Krateros is coming. And he's not happy.”

Perdikkas's face loses even more color. “He didn't know either?!”

The only ones who knew about his pregnancy were his mother, Hyacine, Castorice, and Cipher. “No one was going to react in the best way. Like now.”

Hyacine and Castorice congratulated him instantly. Castorice talked about how she'd been improving at crocheting and how she'd love to make baby clothes, while Hyacine chatted about the care he should take during his pregnancy and how she herself would be his personal doctor. 

Cipher, on the other hand, laughed about how the Deliverer Boy had finally hit the right spot and how she hoped to see little cubs running around everywhere. Maybe she could teach them some of her “tricks”.

Mydei thanked Castorice, took note of everything Hyacine told him, and threw a cucumber at Cipher. She screamed.

(“Did you see that? That's pregnancy mood swings in action!”

“I'll show you the real pregnancy mood swings if you keep talking.”

“...Please don't stress the baby.”)

Mydei expected those reactions. There wasn't a world where his friends wouldn't support him, and vice versa.

What he didn't expect was his mother's reaction. He was prepared for a good scolding for wanting to hide his pregnancy until he was ready to tell everyone, but instead, his mother laughed.

“How much more do you want to be like me, my darling?” She had asked, pinching his cheek as if he were still a child. “Your father boasted a lot about that time, but he never told you about the first two months when I decided to keep it a surprise.”

His mother's support is a balm to his heart.

Not like his friends' dramatic ass reaction. He sighs.

Although he finds it quite amusing that it took those fools so long to realize, because even though he didn't talk about his pregnancy, he never really hid the symptoms.

“I don’t understand how your husband agreed to let you continue the tour,” Ptolemy said, giving up on calming Perdikkas and deciding instead to fan himself. “That man moves heaven and earth if you get sick. It’s a miracle you’re even here without him glued to your back.”

Oh.

Of course, that part.

Mydei doesn't respond, and the room freezes.

Peucesta, the only one who hadn't said a word since everything came to light, stops moving, turns to look Mydei straight in the eyes, and oh.

“Khaslana knows, right, Mydeimos?”

Mydei knows he’s fuck up.

Because even though Hephaestion is the oldest among them, none of them really take his words or scoldings seriously, all too used to his overprotective, mother-hen-like personality. Peucesta, on the other hand, is the one who keeps everyone in line, and seeing him angry can be terrifying.

So, Mydei hugs his belly, thinks of chimeras and cats to give himself strength, says, “Not yet,” and mentally braces himself for the onslaught of scolding from the others, especially Hephaestion.

God, he hopes Phainon is having a better day than he is.

“Krateros fainted?!”

“No, but I'm sure I almost sent him to the hospital from the fright.”

“That old man was in the military, he can't be that scared of a baby.”

“...Mother says he used to tremble when I was a baby and she'd put me in his arms.”

Cipher's laughter could be heard even with the speakerphone off.

Mydei covers the earpiece and looks at the taxi driver taking him home. He seems too focused on driving to notice Cipher's very loud laughter and his presence. He's grateful for that.

He flatly refused to have his entire band escort him from the music company where they work to his home. So much trouble wasn't necessary. Mydei is perfectly capable of going wherever he wants; he doesn't need five "knights in shining armor" on his heels (for that position, there's his husband)

In any case, as long as he keeps his black sunglasses on, a black mask covering his face and his blonde hair tucked under his hat, no one should be able to easily recognize him.

When he hears Cipher calm down enough, he brings the phone closer again.

“Well, little prince, you certainly made quite a scene today, didn’t you? I’m very proud! Keep it up!”

“You’re exaggerating.”

“I literally saw the news that your world tour was cancelled on every TV channel, all morning.” Cipher hums happily. Mydei can just imagine her smiling that cat-like grin of hers. “No one's ready for the biggest surprise! Give them a cool name so that everyone will remember it.”

Mydei hasn't even thought far enough ahead to choose names yet. And he adores Phainon, but his husband is terrible with names. “I'm open to suggestions.”

“Barthol-”

“No.”

“You don't even let me finish.”

Which Mydei finds wonderful, that the world knows that this man is his and Mydei is his, but right now he is undercover, so he cannot boast about Phainon now, unfortunately.

“Let's bet.”

“In these kinds of matters? Nope! 1500 credits. Deliverer Boy names the baby something that matches his dog's.”

Poor Snowy. Mydei thinks his name is cute. Definitely much cuter than Bartholos. “Your expectations are underground.”

“Come on! Spoil me. This girl has to pay the rent for the month.”

“...You're rich. And you live in your own house.”

“And with all the gifts I have planned for that baby? Not for long!”

He knows he'll regret this. Cipher always knows how to turn all her bets in her favor. Even so, “2000 credits. I won't let it be that bad.”

“Deal! It's always a pleasure doing business with you, little lion~”

“...” There's a terrible idea lurking in his head. He thinks about it once, twice, three times, and yet he still acts on it, “My husband might not be good at naming, but he's good at other things.”

“Ha! Like what? Make salads?”

Mydei's smile feels wild. “Like keeping me very satisfied in our bed.”

Cipher's disgusted squeal overlaps with the screech of the taxi's tires as it brakes suddenly, before moving forward again almost a second later. As if the driver had been caught off guard before regaining his senses.

Maybe a cat walked past the taxi, though that doesn't explain the driver's red ears.

Never mind. Cipher is really loud in his ear now. “Eww!! Gross!!” Cipher gags loudly into the phone. Mydei's smile widens. “You two are disgusting.”

“Thanks.”

Cipher makes more gagging sounds just to further emphasize her disgust. “That man is a bad influence on you. Where is my innocent little lion? My kitten from the same litter? We are two innocent kittens against the world!”

“Enough, you sound like Hepha,” Mydei pauses briefly before continuing. “And innocent… Ha! Not even you believe that.”

Cipher's chuckle only confirms it. “A slight exaggeration on my part, the point still stands.”

Mydei was going to continue the conversation. Sometimes he barely has time to talk to his friends, and he's taking advantage of having so much time now thanks to the baby.

That is, until the driver interrupts him. “S-Sir, we'll arrive at your destination in ten minutes.”

Oh well. Perhaps he can call Cipher later. If he's lucky, he'll be able to contact both Castorice and Hyacine at the same time.

He's about to say goodbye when Cipher speaks first. “What a way to tell me to shut up, eh? Don't worry, little lion! Aunt Cipher will be there to ensure your baby has a bright future.”

“I forbid you from teaching them to steal.”

“It's called provoking people into giving me their things!”

“I forbid you from teaching them to manipulate.”

“Tch, you'll see that your second or third baby will follow in my footsteps.”

Mydei's heart takes a dangerous turn. “No— There is no second or third baby…”

“Oh~? But I bet that man of yours will be ready to give your baby a sibling or two as soon as you tell him—”

Mydei hung up immediately before Cipher could delve any deeper into that scenario. Mydei knows she's laughing at him right now, but that's better than her giving him more ideas.

Because just thinking about Phainon being so excited about getting Mydei pregnant that he decides to put another baby in his womb, even though his womb is already full of their child. The burning gaze in those deep blue eyes that he would give him when Mydei told him that he desperately wanted to get pregnant again after their first baby was born, ready to take Phainon at any moment…

Mydei feels his face flush quickly and unconsciously crosses his legs to prevent a small squirt from staining the seats. He prays to Nikador that he really didn't make a mess. Here. In public.

God, these last few days his body feels feverish at the mere thought of spending a good time with his husband. Hyacine told him about the increased libido that comes with entering the second trimester of pregnancy, but Mydei didn't expect it to affect him so much.

Mydei is almost certain it's because he hasn't let Phainon go beyond giving him a few deep, passionate kisses and caresses over his clothes. His eyes darted to the rearview mirror. The taxi driver is looking at him with genuinely concerned eyes, but so noticeably nervous. Mydei's heart sinks, horrified.

There's no way he could have been so careless. “Everything's fine.”

The driver hesitates, uncomfortably. “Sir, your ears are very red, and you were breathing heavily a few moments ago... if you need me to take you to the hospital, I can—”

He doesn't know what the hell the driver saw—Mydei really doesn't want to know—to make him open his eyes so wide and stop looking at him completely. The driver stammers when he speaks to him again.

“I-It doesn't matter. You'll be at your destination in five minutes.”

Mydei is about to jump out the window. “...You said we'd be there in ten minutes a moment ago—”

The silence that followed was the most uncomfortable thing Mydei had experienced in years.

When Mydei opens the door to his home, a nice apartment he and Phainon got a week after getting married, he's not greeted by his loving, cheerful husband. Instead, he's met by a mass of white fur that won't stop barking and jumping.

Mydei smiles, crouching down to the Samoyed's level, carefully avoiding putting any weight on his belly. The dog barks more excitedly as Mydei begins to stroke its head.

“Hey, Snowy. Did you miss me that much?”

The dog barks louder in response. Mydei chuckles softly.

He always feels something warm and welcoming when he returns home. There's so much of Mydei and Phainon everywhere: some antique or instrument in one corner, some brightly colored T-shirt or tight gym shirts in another, and maybe some dubious souvenir from Phainon's travels and some gift from Mydei's fans. The walls and shelves are covered with photos of them, their friends and family; from their college years, their dates, and their wedding. It's large enough to comfortably accommodate two grown men, and it's located on the first floor of the building so they have the privilege of owning their own yard and Snowy can run free.

They don't spend much time at home, but it's always their safe haven to return to. It's perfect for them.

But maybe it's not quite right for a baby.

Mydei sighs, tired of his own thoughts. It's not the time to think about that. He looks at Snowy and, subconsciously, thinks about his conversation with Cipher moments ago.

“Your name is cuter.” That's all he says before patting Snowy's silky fur one last time and standing up.

He heads to his room, changes into Phainon's favorite oversized yellow hoodie, and goes to the living room, collapsing onto the sofa with nothing to do. Snowy follows him everywhere, trying to get more cuddles like the clingy dog he is, which only makes Mydei think about Phainon again.

He checks his phone, knowing there won't be any messages at this hour. That doesn't stop the small, disappointed "hmph" he lets out when he sees messages from his manager, from Krateros, from the group chat with his band—from everyone except his husband.

He puts his phone away and, in the silence that follows, delves deeper into his thoughts once more.

The thing is, Mydei and Phainon don't see each other much.

Their jobs keep them apart more often than they'd like. When Phainon is home (which is rare), Mydei is playing with his band, traveling to other cities, and spending days in the studio practicing and writing new songs. When Mydei is home (even rarer), chances are Phainon is flying long commercial routes and sleeping at airline bases.

Having a long-distance relationship is difficult for both of them, especially since they were so inseparable when they were younger. The time differences, their busy schedules, the days or weeks they don't see each other in person—it can be exhausting.

That doesn't mean they don't try to stay in touch. Phainon always tries to send a good morning and good night message, though Mydei usually receives it in the afternoon.  On the other hand, Mydei sends him pictures of his day, whether it's what he had for dinner or what he's wearing, knowing full well that Phainon won't reply until many hours later with a barrage of messages responding to everything. 

They try to call each other during the week, when they know the other isn't busy, and they video chat every weekend, though it's often just to see each other or watch a movie. They plan their days off together, which means Phainon has the last two weeks of each month free to relax at home, and Mydei manages to join him during the second week of his vacation.

They make it work. It's been their routine for almost two years now since they got married.

What would it be like now with a baby on the way? 

“When the baby arrives, you won't be able to run all over the house," he tells Snowy. The dog probably doesn't understand what he's saying, or maybe he does, because his ears are flat against his head and he's giving him that beaten-puppy look. "Don't look at me like that, you have a whole yard out there."

Snowy whimpers.

…Would their baby be an exact copy of Phainon, just as Phainon looks so much like Snowy, or would they look more like Mydei?

Would they have big blue eyes or sharp golden ones? Snow-white hair or strawberry blonde? Phainon's sunny smiles or Mydei's smaller ones? Soft, easy-to-read expressions or more reserved and stoic ones?

Perhaps their baby will be born with their father's two antennae of hair…

Almost as if he'd been summoned, his cell phone buzzes with the special message tone Phainon had created for himself. When he reaches for his phone, he ignores all other messages and opens the chat with the white-haired man.

Grown ass man is still sending kaomojis at almost 30 years old.

That brings a smile to Mydei's face and, unconsciously, he plays with his braid.
